incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — increased 5xxs from decode streaming path, elevated CUDA OOMs on nvdecode-pool-3. Paging oncall now: @Rohan (pager)
Rohan (oncall): On it. Joining triage. Any immediate impact numbers? Who's on runtime? @Alice?
Alice (runtime): Seeing a burst of `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` on decode shards. Logs show repeated unbounded token generation on streaming sessions. Suspect max_tokens not being enforced in the gateway -> decoder path.
Ben (support): We started getting customer reports ~5m ago: multiple dropped streams and `500` for chat completions. One customer reported session hung then dropped. Ticket #54891 created.
Eve (prodops): Stack: nginx gateway -> traffic-proxy -> router -> decoder-service(gpu). The router logs show `max_tokens=0` in some requests; downstream decoder treats 0 as "unset" -> unlimited. That lines up with runaway generations.
Rohan (oncall): Can we throttle or reject right now? We need an immediate mitigation to stop OOM cascade.
Alice (runtime): Quick mitigations:
- Apply server-side hard cap on tokens for streaming endpoints (50k -> 512 default) at router level (hotfix)
- Blackhole traffic to the affected decoder pool and shift to fallback smaller-ram variant
- Restart one pod to clear stuck allocations
I'll push a config change to enforce `max_tokens <= 4096` at router. That should block new runaway sessions.
Carol (eng-runtime): +1. Also disable prefix/KV cache on fallback variant to reduce memory footprint. Who can roll the router config? @Eve?
Eve (prodops): I can push a hotpatch to router config. Will do a canary to 5% first then 100% if green. Deploybot will post status.
deploy-bot: Starting rollout: router-hotpatch/max_tokens_cap -> canary(5%)
Alice (runtime): Adding a short circuit in decoder: if header `x-client-max-tokens` present and > 10000, clamp to 4096 and log. Also returning 429 with clear message if client explicitly requests > 4096.
Ben (support): Noted — we'll update the tickets and let affected customers know we're throttling requests to prevent instability. Any estimate on requests dropped so far?
Alice (runtime): Preliminary numbers: ~1.3k streams failed in the last 6 minutes, ~480 distinct clients, peak GPU mem pressure at 92% on nvdecode-pool-3, several pod restarts observed, two container crashes registered with OOM kill.
Rohan (oncall): Severity P1 due to customer impact & infrastructure instability. Escalating to eng-runtime lead @Carol. Carol, do you want SRE involvement for capacity adjustments or failover logic?
Carol (eng-runtime): Yes. SRE, please redirect router traffic away from nvdecode-pool-3 and bring up extra fallback instances in nvdecode-small pool. Also collect full heap dumps and decoder trace logs.
Eve (prodops): Doing traffic shift now -> moving 30% -> 70% over next 2min. Spinning up 6 small-fallback replicas.
Alice (runtime): Attaching log snippet from decoder pod (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T09:07:12Z] ERROR decode_worker.cpp: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
stack: decode_loop -> kv_cache_grow -> allocate_workspace -> cudaMalloc
request_id=xyz-7b3
payload: {"stream_id":"abc","max_tokens":0}
```
Ben (support): Customers impacted: 3 enterprise accounts reporting degraded SLA, others are SME-level. Raising to account execs.
Rohan (oncall): Any sign this is malicious or a client bug? 0 as max_tokens seems odd.
Alice (runtime): Root cause theory: protobuf/gRPC proto for GenerationRequest uses `uint32 max_tokens = 4;` where `0` was intended as unspecified. Upstream gateway used `0` to mean unlimited in previous old behavior. The decoder interprets `0` as "no cap". Regression introduced in gateway update last week where we stopped sending `max_tokens` field when unset; some clients set `0` intentionally. So mismatch in semantics -> runaway.
Carol (eng-runtime): Action items:
- immediate: router hotpatch (enforced cap) — Eve
- immediate: shift traffic & scale fallback — Eve/SRE
- rollback gateway change that stopped omitting the field OR normalize semantics in proto handling — Alice
- add unit test for proto default handling — Alice
- customer comms & health checks — Ben
Rohan (oncall): Agreed. Carol, can you coordinate a rollback if hotpatch insufficient?
Carol (eng-runtime): I'll be ready. If canary shows any residual OOMs after cap enforcement, we'll roll back last gateway deploy at revision r2026-03-08.
Eve (prodops): Router canary at 5% looks good so far (no new OOMs on canary traffic). Increasing to 100% now.
deploy-bot: Router hotpatch rollout: canary(5%) -> 100% succeeded.
Alice (runtime): After cap enforcement, observed immediate drop in new OOM events. GPUs stabilizing: nvdecode-pool-3 now 55% mem.
Ben (support): Triage complete for immediate mitigation. Notifying affected customers with a short incident note and ETA for full fix.
Rohan (oncall): Handing off to Carol for root cause fix / postmortem. I'll sign off from pager in 30min unless there are regressions.
Carol (eng-runtime): Taking over. We'll schedule a postmortem, include timeline, root cause, and action items (proto semantics doc, gateway bugfix, router caps, alerting updates). Assign owners: Alice -> code fix & tests, Eve -> deploy verification, Ben -> customer comms.
Alice (runtime): I'll open PR to normalize proto handling and add a defensive check in decoder to treat `0` as `unset` and require explicit `unbounded=true` flag for unlimited. PR #4120
Ben (support): I'll bundle customer impact numbers and update #54891 with root cause summary and mitigation steps.
Rohan (oncall): Marking this incident closed for pager purposes. If anything pops, ping me.
Carol (eng-runtime): Postmortem timeline: doc + draft by EOD tomorrow. Follow-ups: add metric for "requests with max_tokens=0" and alert if > 10/minute.
Eve (prodops): Will also add a throttling policy in infra for streaming endpoints as a safety net.
incidents-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> routing caps applied, traffic shifted, decoder restarts completed. Severity downgraded to P2. Incident record: IR-2026-0315-01
Alice (runtime): Small follow-up: we saw one lingering crashed container with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` during high churn; file included in runbook.
Ben (support): Customers notified, a few asked for postmortem copy. Will circulate when ready.
Carol (eng-runtime): Thanks everyone. Good catch/fast actions. We'll keep the ticket open until RC deployed and tests in prod pass.
Rohan (oncall): Thanks team. Signing off now. :thumbsup:
